observations: The sheet uses a large black serif title, white space, thin horizontal rules, and numbered sections for target devices, sizes, grayscale, fonts, components, and prohibited patterns.

The visible font labels specify Noto Serif SC 900 for titles and book names, Noto Sans SC 400/500/700 for interface and body text, and Literata 400/600/700 for numerals and Latin text. These are printed reference labels, not a verification of installed or rendered fonts.

The eight visibly labelled grayscale tokens are #000, #555, #666, #999, #BBB, #DDD, #EEE, and #FFF. Their listed roles distinguish text and selected controls, secondary text, read chapters, disabled text, dots and borders, thin dividers and tracks, state highlights, and paper. The sheet states 16 grayscale levels and 0x11 increments.

The printed Paperwhite/Scribe sizing table gives minimum touch values 48/56, title sizes 34/46, book or list-title ranges 17-22/19-30, body or button ranges 15-17/17-19, annotation ranges 12-14/13-15, page margins 22/36, and shelf grids 4x2/6x3. These are read specification values; no native pixel geometry was measured.

The printed rule system distinguishes a 1-unit thin rule, a 1.5-unit control outline, and a 2-unit popup outline. The corner row gives 4 for general corners and 2 for tags, and rejects capsule shapes. The component samples show black primary buttons, white outlined secondary buttons, selected versus unselected segments, tag states, list rows, source switching, a bounded toast, and pagination.

The prohibited-pattern panels visibly reject scrolling lists, animation and transitions, shadows or scrims or gray backdrops, and capsule or hover or overly thin styling. The grayscale section also states hardware inversion for night mode. These are source-reference observations, not newly proposed product capabilities.

observations: Four reader diagrams visibly distinguish right-to-left paging, left-to-right paging, vertical or long-strip reading, and Scribe landscape two-page reading. Side next/previous regions reverse with reading direction; each diagram retains a middle menu region. The vertical diagram states scrolling 85% while retaining 15%, and the Scribe landscape caption states a 40% middle menu region.

The readable prose says turning regions are inactive while the menu is open, a center or blank-area tap closes it, and advancing past a chapter's final page enters the next chapter with a full refresh. The diagrams communicate reference interaction intent; they do not establish live hit regions or physical input results.

The refresh table visibly separates fast button feedback using A2/DU, ui updates using GL16, partial comic paging using REAGL/GL16, full reader or chapter transitions using GC16, and fast-to-partial progress dragging. Its comic row lists a default full-refresh interval of 6 with options 1/3/6/10/chapter-only. The keyboard row states feedback within 100 ms, the cover-loading row states 300 ms batching, and the night row uses hardware inversion. These are printed contracts, not measured timings or observed waveforms.

The visible ui rows describe bounded refresh rectangles for dialogs and toasts, unchanged underlying content, and an upward-expanding page-number panel. The table's footer states fallback to GL16 where a device does not support a mode.

The gesture table visibly gives release-triggered taps, a long-press threshold of at least 500 ms, a double-tap threshold below 300 ms, a horizontal-swipe row with 900 ms and 5.6 mm, and a top-edge swipe beginning within 8 mm. Pinch is unused in shelf/list contexts and shown as local reader zoom. The smallest detector-conversion note is not claimed as fully read.

The platform panels are visibly headed by sleep interrupting Wi-Fi, no system keyboard, no web component, WASM source modules, limited memory and CPU, and coexistence with Kindle. Their presence and broad themes were viewed; the smallest wrapped implementation prose remains pending.
